agenda_items.title: Chair's Verbal Update
agenda_items.minutes:
Ādisōke Update
Chair Luloff highlighted recent construction progress on the Central branch at Ādisōke, including exterior landscaping work, wood cladding, feature staircases, custom millwork, as well as framing, tiling, light fixtures, and painting. He encouraged everyone to follow the project online.
Branding Launch - Billboards and Transit Signage
Chair Luloff announced that a transit ad campaign to promote OPL’s new brand will occur in April and May. The campaign will introduce the new brand, increase the visibility of OPL, and build public awareness of OPL in Ottawa’s busiest areas.
Riverside South Public Engagement
Chair Luloff noted that an architect has been engaged and is actively working on the building design and floorplan layout for the Riverside South facility, and OPL and the City of Ottawa will host a public information session about the project on March 24, with an online survey to follow.
March Break Programming
Chair Luloff highlighted OPL’s activities for March Break with the theme of “Curious Creatures.” He further noted teen programming during March Break, including hands-on activities to build practical life skills while having fun. Chair Luloff encouraged clients to browse the full list of programs online.
MOTION OPL 20260310/2
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chair’s verbal update for information.
Results: Received

agenda_items.title: Chief Executive Officer / Chief Librarian (CEO/CL)’s Report
agenda_items.minutes:
Mars est le mois de la francophonie
Sonia Bebbington, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Librarian outlined key programming for Francophonie Month and the Journée internationale de la Francophonie on March 20, including film screenings at library branches. She invited everyone to visit the OPL website for more information.
Romance Author Panel
Ms. Bebbington shared details for the March 26 “Behind the Happily Ever Afters” romance author panel at Bayview Yards which will bring together passionate readers, support a culture of literacy, and strengthen connections with Canadian authors.
One eRead Canada 2026
Ms. Bebbington announced the 2026 One eRead Canada selection is “Ce que je said de toi / What I know about you”, by Éric Chacour, with virtual author talks on April 29 and 30. To learn more about One eRead Canada, visit the OPL website.
Sunnyside Anniversary
Ms. Bebbington announced that Sunnyside branch will celebrate its 75th anniversary on March 28, with official remarks and refreshments at 2:00 pm, as well as activities throughout the day including a magic show, face painting, button making, and a visit from Zoo Crew animals. Registration is required for the activities; please visit the website.
Upcoming Closures
Ms. Bebbington noted that all OPL locations will be closed April 3 and April 6 to observe Good Friday and Easter, and that the 10 branches with Sunday hours, as well as InfoService, will be open on Sunday, April 5. Online resources are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year.
MOTION OPL 20260310/3
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chief Librarian/CEO’s report for information.
Results: Received

sub_agendas_items.title: Community Development Priority Neighbourhood Project
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Sonia Bebbington, CEO/CL, introduced Sarah Macintyre, Division Manager, Client Services, and Robin Gallagher, Program Manager, Client Experience and Community Development who delivered a presentation (held on file with the Chief Executive Officer/ Chief Librarian) updating the Board on the Community Development Priority Neighbourhood Project in the St-Laurent branch service area in 2025. The following is a summary of the information presented:
Chair Luloff said that while the community development approach, and the pilot, initially felt nebulous to him, the presentation clarified how this is an excellent, community‑building initiative. He praised the detailed report and the clear explanation of the work and expressed how pleased he was with the results, adding that the right leadership was in place to support this work.
Rawlson King commended staff for their strong work over the past 10 months, noting he has been impressed by the pilot’s development and its positive impact in the community. He highlighted the value of seeing the community development librarian actively engaging with local residents and emphasized that library branches in high‑priority neighbourhoods provide essential social infrastructure. He noted that community‑embedded models for library service, which he learned more about at a past American Library Association conference, are proven to improve early literacy, digital inclusion, newcomer integration, and service use. He cited the significant increases in bookmobile usage in his ward and praised the librarian’s responsive programming at the St-Laurent community centre. He concluded by asking about the range of partners supporting the pilot. Ms. Gallagher responded by outlining key partnerships, including with Ottawa Public Health (OPH), the City’s Recreation, Cultural and Facility Services Department, the Integrated Neighbourhood Services Team, and the Integrated Departmental Task Force (the latter two both within Community and Social Services Department at the City) to coordinate support.
Rawlson King underscored the importance of coordination among partners to avoid working in silos and to create more effective solutions and noted the visible presence of OPL at local events like Overbrook Day and community association meetings as well as ongoing connection and engagement with the community.
Rawlson King asked about engagement with Indigenous urban residents, noting the importance of including First Nations and especially Inuit community members in equity‑informed service delivery. Ms. Gallagher explained that Indigenous engagement is guided by the Indigenous Services team at OPL and follows a rights‑based, community‑led approach. Rawlson King validated the need to work at the community’s chosen pace, remarked that it is important for Ottawa’s Indigenous community to be at the table, and thanked staff for their efforts, stating that the pilot reflects OPL’s core mission by delivering trusted, accessible services where they are most needed.
Alison Crawford asked whether more detailed information was available about residents’ information needs from OPH and collaborations with OPL, as mentioned in the presentation, and further inquired what data the team plans to collect in the coming year. Ms. Macintyre indicated she would follow up on the public health question and further explained that next year data will continue to track quantitative measures, such as program and bookmobile attendance, card registrations, and offsite participation, while placing greater emphasis on client outcomes.
Alison Crawford inquired about collaboration with the Vanier branch team, particularly with respect to engagement with Indigenous clients and residents. Ms. Macintyre explained that the pilot focused on St-Laurent branch because the priority neighbourhood identified in the analysis falls within this branch service area. Noting that branches do not work in isolation, she further underscored that one of the aims of this work is to embed successful partnerships into regular operations across more communities, serving as a model for expansion.
There being no further discussion, the presentation was RECEIVED as presented.
MOTION OPL 20260310/4
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the presentation for information.
Results: Received

sub_agendas_items.title: 2026 Ontario Library Association Super Conference – Reports from Vice-Chair Kathy Fisher and Harvey A. Slack

attachments.attachment_title: 2026 OLA Conference - Report from Vice-Chair Kathy Fisher and Harvey A. Slack.pdf

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Harvey A. Slack reported on his experience attending the Ontario Library Association conference, calling it a valuable opportunity to connect with library workers and supporters from across Ontario, other provinces, and the U.S. He noted the enthusiastic response to OPL’s new logo and highlighted strong presentations by OPL staff, including Sarah Macintyre. He said he learned a great deal from the sessions and encouraged others to attend future conferences, emphasizing the value of sharing ideas with peers. He concluded by noting that libraries are increasingly becoming the “living rooms” of their communities, a theme echoed throughout the conference.
There being no further discussion, the report was RECEIVED as presented.
MOTION OPL 20260310/7
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the report for information.
Results: Received
